correctedFindings.finding: Member.displayName was empty against the canonical field map
correctedFindings.detail: The field map sources the name from gateway.identity_mappings through an authorized Gateway identity read. No identity readback RPC exists in packages/contracts/proto/internal.proto, and no migration in this repository creates gateway.identity_mappings (services/gateway-integration/migrations/0001_opl_tenant.sql creates only the tenant schema). The Gateway HTTP adapter exposes only the caller's own /api/v1/auth/login and /api/v1/auth/me; the Sub2API admin user lookup requires a Cloud service credential, which 02_database_schema_complete.md forbids using to act as a member ("不用Cloud服务令牌冒充成员"). The field therefore stays empty rather than being invented, and the contract was not edited to declare it optional.

correctedFindings.finding: the invitee owner entry was described as reusing AuthorizeAction while it checked the session directly
correctedFindings.detail: Two defects. (1) authorizeInvitee performed its own session check instead of the shared path; it now builds the same typed request and calls AuthorizeAction. (2) The ACCEPTINVITATION branch in AuthorizeAction returned early and ignored any authorization context the caller presented, so a context issued for another action was silently discarded rather than verified. Context verification is now one shared routine (verifyOriginalContext) used by both the invitee branch and every other action, so a present context must match actor, session, scope, permission version, expiry, action and resource or the request is denied.

correctedFindings.finding: the seven-day invitation window was an implementation choice presented as if it were spec
correctedFindings.detail: No canonical value exists anywhere in docs/spec/target: 02_database_schema_complete.md only derives the invitation status from expires_at. The hardcoded constant was removed; the owner now takes the window as explicit configuration (OPL_INVITATION_TTL) and refuses to start without a positive value, following the instance-approved UploadPolicy precedent rather than inventing product policy. The persisted expiresAt is the configured window, and the expiry boundary is proven by TestInvitationExpiryBoundaryPostgres.

correctedFindings.finding: the member front end was attributed to W14
correctedFindings.detail: W13 (Console/BFF basic integration, F01) owns the login/member surface; W14 is the agent/upload/build front end (F02-F06). docs/roadmap.md and docs/status.md no longer claim W14 for the member page.

unprovenItems: Member.displayName has no authorized source yet; the field is emitted empty and the item stays open.

getWorkspaceAccess is not authorized at all: 03_api_contract_complete.yaml assigns it x-owner: workspace (x-tables: workspace.workspaces, F09) while internal.proto declares it on ServeProductService. A serve-audience row would contradict the contract and a workspace-audience row would serve an owner this policy does not cover, so no row exists and policy_generated_test.go pins that absence. Resolving it needs a canonical-owner decision.

OPL_INVITATION_TTL is a new required deployment configuration value. The deploy manifests and the instance profile were not edited (instance-owned), so an existing deployment that enables invitations must add it before this revision would start.
No Console member page exists; only the BFF REST surface is implemented.
Tenant onboarding, suspend/reenable, delete/restore, retained-identity migration and Gateway wallet binding remain unimplemented.
No production, Candidate, Release, Instance qualification or real Sub2API account was touched.
failedAttempts: Three focused test failures surfaced during this round and were resolved rather than worked around: a platform administrator acting on an explicit tenant scope was wrongly expected to be denied (SSOT 02_database_schema_complete.md:143 permits it, so the test expectation was corrected); a second invitation was issued to a subject that already owned a Tenant (test data corrected); and the repeat-acceptance case reused a pre-acceptance session struct instead of re-reading the live session the way the BFF does.

A contract-consistency Go test that re-derived the table from the YAML contract was abandoned because it would have required adding a YAML dependency to the gateway-integration Go module; the committed tests assert the per-owner surface and the exact audience/roles instead, without a new dependency.

logAvailability.note: output/ is listed in .gitignore, so these logs are local-only artifacts rather than checked-in files. The sha256 values above bind them; an independent verifier reproduces them by re-running the same commands on this SHA with an isolated PostgreSQL admin DSN. The logs contain no credential: the isolated admin DSN is written only as a placeholder, and no browser cookie, password, Gateway token or invitation token is printed.
